title: Cameroun Poulet DG: Chicken for the Director General (Yummy Medley)
author: Lois (Yummy Medley)
desc: Chicken thigh cubes marinated at least 30 minutes in a blended cilantro, celery and Scotch bonnet marinade, broiled, then combined with fried plantain rounds, carrots, bell peppers and a reduced tomato sauce.
longDesc: Lois, a non-Cameroonian blogger, learned this from a Cameroonian friend, Joyce, and notes its similarity to a Nigerian dish. The chicken is marinated at least 30 minutes in half the blended marinade. Plantain rounds (1 cm) are fried golden on both sides; the chicken is broiled until golden brown without flipping; the onion is sautéed 5 minutes until translucent; blended tomatoes are reduced on high heat until thick; the reserved marinade is added and simmered 5 minutes. Carrots cook 5 minutes, then the plantains, chicken and bell peppers 5 more minutes. The page notes that unripe plantains darken more than ripe ones.
ingredients: 3 shallots or half a red onion
1 1/2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs, chopped into 1-inch cubes
1/2 green, 1/2 yellow, 1/2 orange bell pepper, cut into strips
steps: Blend the marinade ingredients. Marinate the chicken at least 30 minutes in half of it; keep the rest.
Fry 1 cm plantain rounds until golden on both sides.
Broil the chicken until golden brown, without flipping. (The broiler temperature is not printed.)
Sauté the onion about 5 minutes on medium heat until translucent. Add the blended tomatoes on high heat and reduce until thick.
Add the reserved marinade and simmer 5 minutes on low-medium heat.
Add the carrots for 5 minutes, then the plantains, chicken and bell peppers for 5 more minutes.
chefTips: Printed cues: chicken ‘golden brown’; onion ‘translucent’; tomato ‘reduce until thick’.
Unripe plantains darken more than ripe ones when fried.
The broiler temperature is not printed.
commonMistakes: Crowding the plantains in the pan.
Cooking the bell peppers too long.
healthBenefits: Chicken thighs, plantains and vegetables in one dish.
culturalNote: The page says the dish is usually served on special occasions in Cameroon and compares it to Nigerian gizdodo. The author is not Cameroonian and learned it from a Cameroonian friend named Joyce.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Cameroun Poulet DG: Chicken for Director General’. Byline as printed: ‘Lois’ / ‘By Lois (Yummy Medley)’ (the print page says ‘Yummy Medley’). Dates differ between the two extractions and are not reconciled: ‘10 Jun 2017, updated 23 Dec 2019’ in one, ‘Apr 9 2015, updated Jul 12 2025’ in the other. Yield 4–6. Ingredients TWO-PASS (quoted); method paraphrased on both passes.
ABSENT: broiler temperature; times (prep and cook are placeholders built from the stated 30-minute marinade and the 5-minute steps).
